newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. chief tells Guatemalan rebels to make amends.
newsitem.headline: U.N. chief tells Guatemalan rebels to make amends.

text.p: U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali on Tuesday deplored the kidnapping by leftist Guatemalan rebels of an 86-year old woman, saying it endangered the peace process in the Central American country.

"He calls on the Guatemalan National Revolutionary Unit or URNG to take all action necessary to restore conditions in which a final peace agreement can be reached promptly in Guatemala," chief U.N. spokeswoman Sylvana Foa said.

"He is greatly concerned by the kidnapping. He deplores this incident and the damaging consequences for the peace negotiations under the auspices of the United Nations, which are very close to a successful conclusion," she said.
The Guatemalan government suspended peace talks planned for Tuesday, saying the kidnapping by a URNG guerrilla commander violated terms of the peace process.
The move came as a surprise in light of expectations that the government and the URNG would sign a definitive peace accord by December, thereby bringing an end to Guatemala's 36-year-old civil war.

The talks were thrown off track after police on Oct. 19 arrested Rafael Augusto Valdizon Nunez, also known as "Comandante Isaias," leader of one of four separate guerrilla armies that make up the URNG, on suspicion of kidnapping.

According to government officials, Valdizon admitted men under his command were holding 86-year-old Olga Alvarado de Novella, kidnapped Aug. 25. Valdizon negotiated his freedom in exchange for giving up Alvarado.
